# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question.
- When several nearby strings look similar, first locate the question's printed label or identifier, then read only the value bound to it: the entry in the same row and the same column as the requested header, the value directly adjacent to the matching label in the label's own row, or the row whose header matches the identifier. Do not take a value from an adjacent row or column, and do not answer with a similar-looking nearby entry just because it is more legible or prominent; if the label wording or identifier characters do not match the question's terms, move to the next candidate. When several short values share a shape (multiple phone/fax numbers, codes, or coordinates), use the question's label wording to pick one and return only it in its printed form (a coordinate or code stays a code; a telephone number keeps its printed punctuation), with no commentary about rejected alternatives.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible; for action deadlines, apply the scope rule below.
- For questions asking when a form or action must be completed or sent, return the date bound to that completion/submission instruction as an action deadline. If the deadline is expressed as a month and day and a year is only surrounding document context, do not append that year merely because it is visible; return the deadline at month-and-day granularity, preserving the printed month/day order and punctuation. Include a year when the question explicitly asks for a year or full date, or when the year is necessary to identify which visible deadline applies. This scoping applies to completion/submission deadline questions, not to requests for the date written on a document, a birth date, or another date that calls for the full recorded date; those keep the complete printed date. The rule refines the requested span for action deadlines and does not authorize general date shortening, reformatting, or removal of requested date components.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- When the question asks for a person's designation, title, position, or role, return the title/role phrase bound to that person and stop before a comma-separated or otherwise appended division, institute, department, employer, or broader organizational affiliation, unless the question explicitly asks for affiliation or the full organizational address. Preserve the complete wording of the title itself, including rank or official modifiers, but do not append a broader hierarchy merely because it is printed with the title. If the printed designation is an inseparable multi-part official title, keep only the components needed to identify the role. This scope rule must not shorten requested proper names or formal organization names: when the question asks for a person's name, company, university, or another named entity, return the printed full name as requested.
- Return each value in one rendering: if the same quantity is expressed twice (spelled-out words plus a numeral, a numeral plus a parenthetical restatement, or two equivalent currency renderings), use the single main printed entry and do not append an equivalent in parentheses, brackets, or a trailing gloss. Keep the number together with its printed currency/units and any qualifier the question asks about, even when a shorter numeral form also exists. Retain nonduplicate parenthetical content as printed, including an acronym gloss, alternate name, or other parenthetical that is part of a printed name, and a unit or qualifier that changes the meaning. Before finalizing, check that the candidate answer contains the requested value once, in one notation.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
- When the answer is a quoted tagline or slogan and the question asks for the wording rather than glyph-level typography, transcribe the enclosing quotation marks as standard ASCII double quotation marks and keep the quoted words otherwise unchanged. Do not add quotation marks when the answer is not a quoted phrase, and do not apply this convention to names, codes, dates, units, or numeric values. If the question explicitly asks for the exact printed punctuation or glyphs, preserve those instead.

### Polar yes/no answer scope
- When the question is a direct yes/no question (for example, it asks Did/Does/Is/Was/Were/Are/Can/Could/Do/Does/Will/Has/Have and does not also request a detail), return only the polarity word "Yes" or "No" inside the answer element. Do not append the supporting fact, person, institution, year, or a sentence containing the evidence, even when that detail is visible and relevant. Do not add a trailing period or other punctuation after the single word.
- If the question asks for more than polarity (for example, "Did X...? If yes, when/where?" or any question requesting a name, list, date, number, title, quoted phrase, location, or other value), answer the additional requested item at the requested granularity and preserve the full entity/value/phrase. This rule must not shorten non-polar questions or replace a requested answer with a bare yes/no.
